title: Hotpatch requests & stitch notes - urgent asks synthesis
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact synthesis of small-to-medium customer asks we surfaced in Dec 2026 — the ones customers flagged as 'blocking' or 'urgent' for production (not big roadmap features). Goal: make trade-offs explicit, propose short remediations, and capture follow-ups for eng/product.

Context & why this doc exists:
- Most recent CS triage (12/09–12/10) pulled ~23 rapid asks from 8 customers (mid-market + 2 enterprise). Many are variants of observability granularity, policy routing edgecases, and billing attribution mismatches.
- Customers report these impact confidence to run inference at scale more than they impact model quality.
- We need a set of low-risk hotpatches (1–3 sprint scope) that materially reduce friction while we evaluate longer-term product work.

Top recurring problem clusters (quick map):
1) Ambiguous model-routing fallbacks
   - Symptom: when a route-level pin isn't available, customers see fallback to a lower-tier model w/o clear signal in logs; their client code treats all 200 responses as identical and misattributes latency/regression to our model.
   - Representative quote: 'We had a live mismatch for 30 minutes and it cost us a campaign; no trace that fallback occurred.' — Fintech A
   - Severity: high (trust/ops risk)
2) Token-level cost & trace per-request missing
   - Symptom: aggregated token charts are fine, but customers cannot see token counts per user-request (or map tokens to route/feature).
   - Consequence: hard to bill internal product teams and debug cost regressions.
   - Severity: medium-high
3) KV/prefix caching invalidation confusion
   - Symptom: prefix caching TTLs and cache key derivation differ between hosted and private installs; customers see stale outputs and inconsistent latency.
   - Severity: medium
4) Embedding dedup & storage lifecycle ask
   - Symptom: customers want an automated TTL sweep and a low-cost deduping hint to reduce storage spend.
   - Severity: medium-low

Concrete quick-win proposals (minimal infra touch, scoped to 1 sprint where possible):
A) Emit "effective_model_id" and "fallback_reason" in response headers + console traces
   - Why: instantly solves trust & debugging for routing fallbacks.
   - Effort estimate: small runtime change + console display tweak.
   - Owner suggestion: eng-serving-runtime (Jordan) + product-hosted-api (Sophie)
   - Risks: header proliferation; privacy check for private deployments (need approval for header names).

B) Per-request token metadata toggle (opt-in) and export to CSV/console
   - Why: gives teams immediate per-request token visibility without wholesale billing overhaul.
   - Implementation: runtime emits per-request record to internal trace pipeline when flag=true; UI provides CSV export for last 14 days.
   - Effort: small–medium (trace infra + UI).

C) Cache-key doc + default TTL harmonization and a small diagnostic endpoint
   - Why: reduce mismatch across deployments; give customers a way to simulate/inspect cache key derivation.
   - Implementation: product doc + /v1/_debug/cache-key?prompt=... endpoint returning key and TTL computed.
   - Effort: doc + lightweight endpoint.

D) Embedding lifecycle playbook + dedup hint API
   - Why: immediate cost reductions for heavy-embedding customers.
   - Implementation: recommend TTL strategy + add optional 'dedup_hint' field on embedding uploads; backend returns suggested dedup bucket id.
   - Effort: doc + small API additive change.

Prioritization table (short):
- P0: A (fallback tracing headers) — fixes trust/incident surfaces quickly.
- P1: B (per-request tokens opt-in) — high customer value but heavier infra.
- P2: C (cache-key doc + debug endpoint) — low risk, quick UX win.
- P3: D (embedding lifecycle) — valuable but some infra design.

Customer vignettes (short):
- Enterprise X (healthcare): saw silent fallback overnight when eastern region capacity throttled; compliance required audit trail of exact model id and quantization applied. Wants SLO-level evidence per request.
- AI-native startup Y: token spike last week; couldn't attribute to a single feature and temporarily shut off new rollout. Needs per-request token CSV for debugging.
- Marketplace Z: embedding storage ballooned; they want suggestion for cheap dedup before they cost cap out.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Header naming and privacy policy for private deployments: do we allow adding operational headers to user-facing responses in Private mode? (Product/legal).
- Cost of per-request traces: sampling? full capture? our trace pipeline and retention implications (SRE + infra billing).
- Dedup_hint semantics: deterministic vs probabilistic; storage index cost (applies to db team).

Own-the-work proposals (who does what next):
- Product (Sophie): align on header naming, draft rollout notes to affected customers, update roadmap with P0 cold sprint target (Jan sprint).
- Eng-runtime (Jordan + Elias): prototype header emission (local dev) and a small console trace band to show fallback events.
- Observability (Marco): run cost impact analysis for enabling per-request token metadata at 10% sample.
- CS (Asha): craft customer-facing note for top-3 impacted customers with expected timeline and workaround steps.

Short-term customer communication template (to send after internal alignment):
Subject: Update on routing/fallback trace and next steps
Body: Short apology, what we found, what we will ship (fallback headers + console trace), estimated timeline (2–3 weeks for rollout), temporary workaround (set route pin + verify via /v1/models endpoint). Include snippet: response header X-Redwood-Effective-Model: redwood-v1-small | X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason: capacity-throttle.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- [ ] Get legal note on headers in private deployments (GLS).
- [ ] Create RFC sketch for per-request token opt-in (link to JIRA-2147).
- [ ] Add cache-key debug endpoint to eng-sprint board; small doc + example curl.
- [ ] Schedule 30-min sync with SRE to assess trace pipeline cost (Marco + Jordan).

Appendix: raw customer snippets (partial, redacted)
- 'We couldn't tell which model was used; logs looked normal but outputs were cheaper/lower-qual.' — Fintech A
- 'If we could export token usage per user session we could correlate to feature rollout.' — Startup Y
- 'We're willing to accept a disabled-by-default debug mode if it helps us root cause faster.' — Marketplace Z

Quick reference links (internal):

- Triage board: https://linear.app/redwood/board/triage/urgent-asks
- Prototype PR for response headers: https://github.com/redwood/inference-platform/pull/458

End of memo.

(Informal: I sketched header names in the PR; need to double-check private deployment policy. Aiming to present to eng triage Monday 01/11.)
